**The meaning of the verse**
﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُونُوا قَوَّامِينَ لِلَّهِ شُهَدَاءَ بِالْقِسْطِ ۖ وَلَا يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ شَنَآنُ قَوْمٍ عَلَىٰ أَلَّا تَعْدِلُوا ۚ اعْدِلُوا هُوَ أَقْرَبُ لِلتَّقْوَىٰ ۖ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ خَبِيرٌ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ﴾
O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ: stand firmly for the truth, seeking the Face of Allah, as witnesses with justice. And do not let hatred of a people lead you to be unjust. Be just between enemies and loved ones equally, for that justice is closer to fearing Allah. And beware of being unjust. Allah is All-Aware of what you do, and He will repay you for it.

📖 At-Tafsir Al-Muyassar — King Fahd Complex.

**Talk with your child**
1. Samer saw Ghassan's palm touch the trunk first. Why was it hard for him to say "Ghassan"?
2. Wassim was angry with his friend Samer. Did Samer betray his friend when he told the truth? And what did Wassim say when he came to him in the evening?
3. What did Samer gain from being just? (Ghassan apologised to him for the day of the mud, and the boys began saying, "Let's ask Samer," and Ghassan was the first to say it.)

**This week's exercise**
Make your child "the judge" in your home this week: they share out sweets or fruit fairly among their brothers and sisters, and judge a family game. And remind them to be especially fair with anyone who upset them that day.
